historical_context: V&A discusses the movement through industrial production, the status of craft and the quality of everyday objects. It is not a single decorative repertoire.
visual_principles: Relationships between materials, making and use; the close connection between craft and design.
contemporary_application: Make materials and production methods the rationale for visual decisions in a publication or product identity; texture should serve more than decoration.
exercise: Create two covers for the same event: one with hand-drawn motifs and one using typography alone. Explain which material decisions support communication.
limits: Do not equate botanical patterns with the entire movement; acknowledge makers and sources.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: V&A describes Art Nouveau as an international movement that varied across countries and engaged with historical styles.
visual_principles: Flowing lines derived from natural forms, surface composition and the integration of structure and ornament; geometric examples also exist.
contemporary_application: Create an original poster that unites the headline and main image through a shared line system, with a simpler mark for small uses.
exercise: Observe a local plant and develop three abstractions and a poster without copying its photograph.
limits: Do not reduce every example to flowers, curves or the appearance of one artist.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: V&A emphasizes that Art Deco combines historical and modern elements and cannot be reduced to a single origin.
visual_principles: Geometric stylization, linear rhythm, ornament and varied material effects.
contemporary_application: Try stepped forms and rhythmic letter spacing in a cover or event identity; choose a solution that also works in one color.
exercise: Create three versions of the same cover: black and white, and two different color families.
limits: Gold and black are not mandatory. Do not use historical colonial notions of exotic motifs as decoration without context.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: MoMA defines the Bauhaus as an influential art and design school founded in 1919 and closed in 1933, with experimental teaching focused on materials and function.
visual_principles: Material experiments, connections across art and design disciplines, function and production conditions.
contemporary_application: Derive a brand poster, publication cover and animated title from the same modular rules; test those rules in actual use.
exercise: Explore paper, photography and typography separately, then integrate one exploration into a single production system.
limits: The Bauhaus is not a fixed style consisting only of three primary colors and geometric shapes.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: MoMA connects De Stijl with the publication and art/design milieu of 1917; its approach extends beyond painting into other design disciplines.
visual_principles: Planar relationships, horizontal and vertical organization, asymmetrical balance and limited color families.
contemporary_application: Design a cover and carousel system with rectangular modules that accommodate changing headline lengths.
exercise: Solve the same message in six asymmetrical layouts; check whether hierarchy survives when colors are removed.
limits: Do not copy the composition of a familiar work or mistake a color recipe for the movement as a whole.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: MoMA connects Constructivism in the Russian avant-garde with social function, production and the idea of the artist-engineer.
visual_principles: Abstract structure, organization and production; linking visual form with communication and social purpose.
contemporary_application: Organize announcement priorities through information blocks, direction and scale; connect the formation of blocks to the narrative in a motion version.
exercise: Propose three hierarchies for a public-interest message and explain the communication function of each form.
limits: Red, black and diagonals alone do not establish historical Constructivism. Keep its political context visible.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: MoMA connects Suprematism with Malevich and the context of 1915, emphasizing geometric abstraction away from representation.
visual_principles: Simple geometric forms, relationships in space and formal tension rather than representation.
contemporary_application: Develop an original cover or motion styleframe whose balance changes through small adjustments.
exercise: Move three geometric forms to create six different states of tension and balance.
limits: Do not merge it with Constructivism as though they had identical historical aims.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: MoMA presents Dada through its critique of war and social order alongside chance, improvisation and varied media.
visual_principles: Unexpected encounters, combinations that disrupt meaning and questioning established visual authority.
contemporary_application: Build a critical cover composition from your own elements that questions the language of current news.
exercise: Compare a planned composition with one produced through a chance rule; explain how chance changes meaning.
limits: Randomness does not automatically constitute Dada; identify the cultural and political question.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: MoMA materials on Dada describe recombining photographic fragments from printed mass media. The technique is not limited to one movement.
visual_principles: Cutting, overlapping and changing scale and context to create new meaning between images.
contemporary_application: Build a masked, editable cover in Photoshop; evaluate lighting and edge consistency against the visual goal.
exercise: Create two narratives using only three photographs you own or have suitable licenses to use.
limits: Record source rights; use different quality criteria for critical collage and photorealistic compositing.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: Tate explains Surrealism through rational experience, the unconscious, dreams and the pursuit of liberation; it is an international, plural movement.
visual_principles: Unexpected relationships, the uncanny and varied methods such as automatic drawing and writing.
contemporary_application: Create a cover with original object relationships around one central idea; transform the same conceptual relationship in motion.
exercise: Choose an encounter from five minutes of free writing and turn it into a poster with a clear headline hierarchy.
limits: Surrealism is more than flying objects. Do not assume every work uses the same method.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: MoMA exhibition materials explain the importance of graphic and information design within the avant-garde of the 1920s and 1930s.
visual_principles: The page as an open field, asymmetrical relationships between typography and images, and layouts that clarify meaning.
contemporary_application: Create a content-led poster and publication system; preserve information order during transitions between blocks in motion.
exercise: Design the same announcement symmetrically and asymmetrically; compare how easily readers find its headline, place and date.
limits: Asymmetry does not justify illegibility. Do not present a contemporary adaptation as a historical example.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: An official Swiss publication, through a museum curator account, discusses the relationship of this graphic design tradition to education, typography and communication systems.
visual_principles: Grids, consistent hierarchy, typographic systems and organized relationships with images.
contemporary_application: Produce a poster, an eight-page publication and a carousel layout from one master design specification.
exercise: Compare the same content in gridded and free layouts; test especially with a long headline.
limits: Helvetica and claims of cultural neutrality are not mandatory; choose according to font, language and context.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: Tate explains Pop Art through developments centered in Britain and the United States in the 1950s and 1960s that engaged with popular and commercial culture.
visual_principles: Everyday objects, advertising and packaging language, distinct forms and varied approaches to mass culture.
contemporary_application: Design a social series that centers an ordinary object without copying copyrighted characters or branded packaging.
exercise: Show one object through three narratives; explain whether repetition creates meaning or merely changes color.
limits: Do not reduce Pop Art to one artist repetition scheme or comic-book dots.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: Tate discusses Op Art through geometric visual effects connected with perception and color relationships.
visual_principles: Repetition, spacing, scale, contrast and perceptual change.
contemporary_application: Create an original optical field separate from the primary information; plan effect controls and a static alternative for motion.
exercise: Make six comparisons by changing just one variable in the same geometric field.
limits: Check the risk of rapid flashing and discomfort; keep readable text outside optical tension.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: Tate connects Minimalism in art with the United States in the 1960s, simple geometric forms, materials and the presence of the object.
visual_principles: Form, material, repetition, organization and spatial relationships.
contemporary_application: Reduce a cover to essential elements while preserving meaning, information hierarchy and the production surface.
exercise: Take a design through three stages of reduction and record when meaning is lost.
limits: Historical Minimalism in art and minimal design in marketing language are different concepts.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: V&A discusses postmodern design through plural references, questioning modernist assumptions and connecting different cultural registers.
visual_principles: Layered references, debate through historical quotation, irony and controlled visual contrast.
contemporary_application: Juxtapose two visual languages on a magazine cover for a deliberate editorial idea; explain why one dominates.
exercise: Interpret one headline through two stylistic conflicts and explain how the conflict contributes to its meaning.
limits: Do not conclude that anything can be mixed freely; legibility and context remain design decisions.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: Cooper Hewitt explains the Memphis group founded by Ettore Sottsass through postmodern design debates and objects questioning function and decoration.
visual_principles: Playful scale, unexpected color/form relationships, ornament and debate with modernist expectations.
contemporary_application: Create an energetic event identity with original shapes; keep essential information such as date and place in a calm hierarchy.
exercise: Compare an object’s functional diagram with an expressive poster interpretation.
limits: Memphis is a design group, not a name for all postmodernism or every colorful geometric pattern.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: Cooper Hewitt How Posters Work exhibition discusses psychedelic posters of the 1960s among examples of intense visual experience.
visual_principles: Dense patterns, wandering lines, competing colors and text treated as imagery.
contemporary_application: Develop original rhythmic lettering and forms for a music event; keep essential event information independently readable.
exercise: Make one dense and one calm poster; compare how viewers find the message.
limits: Sensory overload and communication goals differ. Avoid flash/strobe in motion and do not trace existing works.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: The Met discusses subject matter, serial production and collaboration among designers, carvers, printers and publishers in Edo-period woodblock prints.
visual_principles: Registered color blocks, relationships between outlines and layers, and serial production.
contemporary_application: Separate outlines and color layers in an original cover; interpret the formation of print layers in motion as a contemporary proposal.
exercise: Add a third layer to a two-color composition; compare alignment with deliberate displacement.
limits: Do not generalize this as Japanese minimalist style or equate digital layers with historical craft.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: The Met treats geometric ornament as one of several decorative forms in Islamic art, with historical and regional diversity.
visual_principles: Repetition, interlacing and expandable arrangements built from circles, squares, stars and polygons.
contemporary_application: Use an original geometric system as a grid or border without reducing an entire culture to one symbol.
exercise: Construct a starting unit and make three controlled variations in scale, repetition and spacing.
limits: Do not copy a historical object pattern exactly or imply geometry has the same meaning in every region.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: The Met emphasizes calligraphy as a means of communicating text as well as organizing visual form; its uses vary by region and period.
visual_principles: Linear rhythm in writing, reading the text and relationships with ground and ornament.
contemporary_application: Create an original lettering composition with an ordinary phrase whose meaning is verified; check readability with a language specialist.
exercise: Compare linear and circular arrangements of one phrase; record meaning and reading order.
limits: Do not use sacred writing as meaningless texture or equate Turkish, Arabic and Persian writing traditions.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: The Smithsonian record connects AfriCOBRA with Black cultural and political agency and community contexts.
visual_principles: Words within images, energetic color and rhythmic patterns connected with the social message of the source work.
contemporary_application: Determine a community project message with the people involved and create an original rhythm of words and colors.
exercise: Create three visual hierarchies for a short community message you wrote.
limits: Do not generalize specific symbols as African patterns or rename the group through an inaccurate dictionary translation.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: The Met connects the movement with modern Black life, migration, cultural expression and international relationships, emphasizing that it has no single formal language.
visual_principles: Plural narratives through everyday life, portraiture and different visual media.
contemporary_application: Develop a publication series about a neighborhood creative life using participant accounts and permitted images.
exercise: Build an original neighborhood narrative with six scenes and explain the viewpoint of each.
limits: Do not reduce the movement to nightlife, one palette or the forms of one artist.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: The Met essay on Egyptian modern art uses this name to discuss calligraphy and geometry within modern art in specific historical contexts.
visual_principles: Relationships between writing, abstraction and historical/cultural positioning.
contemporary_application: Research a cover through the meaning of writing and its current context, beyond its shape.
exercise: Develop three levels of abstraction for a word while preserving its meaning; explain each in terms of readability.
limits: Do not treat this source-specific name as synonymous with Hurufiyya without separate verification.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

title_en: Sabiha Rüştü Bozcalı: publishing and advertising
aliases: Sabiha Rüştü Bozcalı: publishing and advertising
historical_context: SALT makes Bozcalı’s illustration, publishing and advertising practice visible through archives and exhibitions.
visual_principles: Relationships between visual narrative, drawing and printed communication; contextual study through archival objects.
contemporary_application: Build the Turkey design section around named makers, publications and works rather than a single Turkish style.
exercise: Select a SALT record; analyze composition, message and production context without redistributing the image, then propose an original cover for the same problem.
limits: This study of a practitioner is not an art movement. Record rights for the work, image and archival text separately.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: Getty teacher resources offer activities for examining works through visual elements and design principles.
visual_principles: Line, shape, value, texture and space; explaining balance, emphasis, rhythm and visual relationships with evidence.
contemporary_application: Design Critic should first describe observable organization, then separate interpretation from proposed changes.
exercise: Identify five observed features of a poster and explain their effects without simply calling it beautiful.
limits: Critique must not present personal taste as objective error; consider intention and audience.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

historical_context: The Albers Foundation documents a teaching approach that examines color through relationships and experimentation.
visual_principles: The same color can appear different in different surroundings; use comparative experiments.
contemporary_application: Do not finish brand color selection with one HEX value; compare it on light and dark backgrounds and photographs.
exercise: Place the same inner color in two different surroundings; note how perception changes while its measured value stays constant.
limits: Do not confuse this perceptual exercise with a file color-profile error or treat every color meaning as a universal rule of psychology.
filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.
